title: Hunebed D27 in Borger, Netherlands
summary: Just a short walk from the Hunebedcentrum in Borger stands D27, the largest dolmen in the Netherlands. At over 22 meters (74 feet) long and more than 5,000 years old, this megalithic monument was already ancient when Stonehenge was still centuries away. Massive boulders form the tomb, including the heaviest capstone ever used in a Dutch dolmen, estimated to weigh around 20 tons. The monument has fascinated visitors for centuries. In fact, the first documented archaeological excavation of a Dutch dolmen took place here in 1685. Yet D27 still guards its secrets. title: TWA Flight 529 Memorial in Willowbrook, Illinois
summary: On September 1st, 1961, at 2:00 am, TWA Flight 529 took off from Chicago’s Midway Airport for the last leg of its cross-country journey. Originating in Boston, Flight 529 had already stopped in New York, Pittsburgh, and Chicago, with its next scheduled stop being Las Vegas before continuing to Los Angeles. Shortly after takeoff, the plane (a Lockheed Constellation L-049 prop liner) pitched up and stalled out. Unable to be brought back under control, the plane crashed at 2:05 am in a cornfield in what is now Willowbrook, Illinois. title: Alaska’s monster tsunami sent water 1,580 feet up a mountain
summary: A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second-highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area. As glaciers retreat, similar disasters could become a growing danger in mountainous coastal regions.

It could eventually reveal how tiny molecular machines interact inside cells, providing an unprecedented look at the hidden workings of life.
